summary:
The Fiscal Year 2024 Veterans Affairs Major Medical Facility Authorization Act authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to carry out specified Department of Veterans Affairs major medical facility projects in fiscal year 2024, subject to project-specific maximum amounts, and authorizes appropriations for those projects. The Act does not amend the United States Code and does not itself appropriate funds.

Section 1 designates the short title as the “Fiscal Year 2024 Veterans Affairs Major Medical Facility Authorization Act.”

Section 2(a) grants discretionary authority to the Secretary to carry out 11 major medical facility projects in FY2024 at specified locations, each capped at the stated amount: American Lake, Washington, for construction of new specialty care building 201, renovation of building 18, and parking expansion, not to exceed $155,600,000; Dallas, Texas, for mental health clinical space expansion, parking expansion, and land acquisition, not to exceed $93,100,000; El Paso, Texas, for construction of a new health care center and utility plant, not to exceed $759,200,000; Perry Point, Maryland, for replacement of a community living center and parking expansion, not to exceed $274,310,000; Portland, Oregon, for seismic retrofit and renovation of buildings 100 and 101, roadway and site improvements, construction of a new specialty care facility, demolition, and parking expansion, not to exceed $613,000,000; Reno, Nevada, for initiation of replacement of the Sierra Nevada Health Care System medical center, including land acquisition and preliminary site work, not to exceed $223,800,000; San Diego, California, for a new spinal cord injury building, partial renovation of building 1, parking facilities, central utility plant upgrades, and seismic retrofit of existing spinal cord injury building 11, not to exceed $311,700,000; San Francisco, California, for a new research facility, parking structure, and demolition, not to exceed $264,500,000; San Juan, Puerto Rico, for seismic corrections to building 1, a new administrative building, and outpatient clinic and parking structure expansion, not to exceed $370,370,000; St. Louis, Missouri, for phase 1 of bed tower replacement and related clinical, administrative, warehouse, water tower, utility plant, and parking garage work, not to exceed $135,340,000; and West Haven, Connecticut, for a new surgical and clinical space tower, renovation of buildings 1 and 2, and demolition, not to exceed $153,128,000.

Section 2(b) authorizes, but does not appropriate, $3,354,048,000 to the Secretary for FY2024 or the year in which funds are appropriated to the Construction, Major Projects account for the projects authorized in section 2(a).
